attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack essay, stated as his assessment rather than quoted from anyone else.

semantics.note: A firm present-tense observation. The normalised version drops 'by any reasonable measure', which widens the claim's scope. The contract restores that breadth by testing both capability and adoption.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary. Marcus himself said 'any reasonable measure' and pointed to users, so testing adoption alongside capability is not a stretch. Treating 'squandered' as loss of the lead, without judging blame, is reasonable. The weighting between the two measures is evaluator-supplied.

evidence.note: 2023 leaderboard showing GPT-4 in first place. It sets the earlier baseline only and falls outside the observation window.
Independent Artificial Analysis index, dated 18 Nov 2025, puts Gemini 3 Pro above GPT-5.1 and first on 5 of 10 evals. This supports loss of the capability lead.

Primary Similarweb release, 2 Dec 2025: ChatGPT's web traffic share fell to 71.3% against Gemini's 15.1%. Erosion is real, but a large adoption lead remains, which contradicts the 'any measure' breadth.
Secondary news report of the same Similarweb figures, not an independent measurement. It confirms that ChatGPT kept a substantial traffic lead.

reviews.rationale: The capability part holds: an independent index shows Gemini 3 Pro overtaking OpenAI's best model in November 2025. The adoption part fails: in early December ChatGPT still had about 71% of web traffic share against Gemini's 15%, so a sizable lead remained on a central, ordinary measure. Marcus's 'by any reasonable measure' wording is therefore contradicted in its breadth.
